summary: Attacked part 2 of the Number fields and class field theory area — GlobalNumberFields, GlobalQuadraticForms, LocalFieldsRamification, Multiquadratic, NumberFieldArithmetic, PolynomialGaloisGroups and QuadraticFormInvariants, 65 stages. One finding, medium: all seven roadmaps declare an empty prerequisites list while their own prose states three dependencies among them, one of them at declaration level, and 76 per cent of atlas roadmaps do use that field. The library-boundary head is clean: the global quadratic-form theory the area plans — Hasse-Minkowski, the Hasse invariant, Witt consequences, the Hilbert symbol — is genuinely absent from Mathlib, so the roadmap that barely mentions the library is not neglecting it but has little to consume.
checked: Every stage of all seven roadmaps: QuadraticFormInvariants 18, GlobalNumberFields 12, GlobalQuadraticForms 10, NumberFieldArithmetic 8, PolynomialGaloisGroups 8, LocalFieldsRamification 5, Multiquadratic 4 — 65 in all.

Eligibility, measured rather than assumed: none of the 43 papers this session has reviewed routes to any of these seven roadmaps. I computed entanglement across every available area red team before choosing.

The stage-level graph and status, calibrated against the atlas. All 65 stages have empty `requires` and status 'unknown'; atlas-wide those are 669 of 1962 (34 per cent) and 656 of 1962 (33 per cent). Within norms, and not the finding.

Sibling citations, with the direction of each established from the sentence rather than assumed — the check that matters, since a citation can equally name a consumer. Four pairs carry citations. Three run backwards and are genuine dependencies: QuadraticFormInvariants on LocalFieldsRamification ('The general arithmetic of a nonarchimedean local field belongs to the [local-fields-ramification roadmap], and this sublayer consumes it'); NumberFieldArithmetic on LocalFieldsRamification ('[that roadmap] for the precise ValuativeExtension contract consumed below', and 'Every use of the local API of [the Local Fields and Ramification roadmap] is through this instance'); and GlobalNumberFields on NumberFieldArithmetic, at declaration level ('Define idealsPrimeTo m as the reducible abbreviation of NumberFieldArithmetic.idealsAway m.support').

The two citations that run forwards, and so are not dependencies: QuadraticFormInvariants naming GlobalQuadraticForms ('The resulting frozen declaration hilbertSymbol_productFormula is an export to GlobalQuadraticForms'), and LocalFieldsRamification naming NumberFieldArithmetic ('This is a local theorem: [the Number-Field Arithmetic roadmap] consumes it only after passing to a completion'). The latter matters because it resolves what looks like a mutual dependency between those two roadmaps into supplier and consumer, so there is no cycle.

Roadmap-level prerequisites atlas-wide, which is what turns the empty lists from a convention into a finding: 161 of 211 atlas roadmaps (76 per cent) declare at least one prerequisite, and 0 of these 7 do. The sibling Representation theory area shows the field is used where dependencies exist — CharacterTheory declares three, SpinRepresentations three, QuiverRepresentations, LieHighestWeight and CompactGroups two each.

The library boundary, the head that produced the model-theory area's sharpest finding. Mathlib engagement across the seven runs from 101 mentions (NumberFieldArithmetic) and 77 (PolynomialGaloisGroups) down to 2 (GlobalQuadraticForms, Multiquadratic), and the low end looked like a roadmap planning without checking the library. It is not: GlobalQuadraticForms plans places and completions, archimedean signatures, finite-place invariants, Hasse-Minkowski isotropy, representation and isometry, and global classification with Witt consequences, and Mathlib has none of that global theory. Searching the pinned tree, HasseMinkowski, hasseInvariant, WittGroup/WittRing and hilbertSymbol each return zero files, against 42 files for QuadraticForm and 5 mentioning isotropy. So the global layer is correctly planned and the low mention count reflects little to consume rather than neglect.

That QuadraticFormInvariants' references to a Hilbert symbol are consistent with that absence: it names ClassFieldTheory.hilbertProductFormula and exports hilbertSymbol_productFormula, which are Tau Ceti and sibling-roadmap declarations rather than Mathlib ones, matching the zero hits for hilbertSymbol in the library.

Whether any paper in the blueprint routes to these seven roadmaps, which decides whether PROTOCOL section 17's omissions head has paper needs to test against. Checked at route granularity across all 207 paper result files: 0 routes name any of the seven as their roadmap. A crude substring scan first suggested the opposite, returning 31 to 49 matching files per roadmap, but every match sits in a paper's `examined` record or prose — roadmaps considered as a destination and rejected — and none is a route. So the omissions head could be run only against the roadmaps' own targets, and this red team makes no claim about paper needs.

findings.where: The prerequisites field of all seven area roadmaps in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/: GlobalNumberFields, GlobalQuadraticForms, LocalFieldsRamification, Multiquadratic, NumberFieldArithmetic, PolynomialGaloisGroups, QuadraticFormInvariants
findings.claim: All seven roadmaps declare prerequisites: [], so the atlas records this area as seven mutually independent roadmaps with no build order, while the roadmaps' own prose states three dependencies among them. One is at declaration level: GlobalNumberFields defines objects as reducible abbreviations of NumberFieldArithmetic declarations, so it cannot be elaborated before that roadmap exists. A design or build-order job reading the machine-readable field would get the ordering wrong, and a worker starting GlobalNumberFields or QuadraticFormInvariants would discover the dependency only on reading the prose. This is not the atlas convention: 161 of 211 roadmaps (76 per cent) declare at least one prerequisite, and the sibling Representation theory area declares them wherever they exist.
findings.evidence: Empty lists: each of the seven roadmap records in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ has prerequisites: []. The three dependencies, quoted from the roadmaps' own stage descriptions. (1) QuadraticFormInvariants, sublayer 6A, titled 'The local-field substrate, consumed': 'The general arithmetic of a nonarchimedean local field belongs to the [local-fields-ramification roadmap](../LocalFieldsRamification/README.md), and this sublayer consumes it. The normalized valuation is that roadmap's normalizedValuation...'. (2) NumberFieldArithmetic, Layer 5: '[the Local Fields and Ramification roadmap](../LocalFieldsRamification/README.md) for the precise ValuativeExtension contract consumed below', and separately 'Every use of the local API of [the Local Fields and Ramification roadmap] is through this instance'. (3) GlobalNumberFields: 'Define idealsPrimeTo m as the reducible abbreviation of NumberFieldArithmetic.idealsAway m.support, and integralIdealsPrimeTo m as the reducible abbreviation of NumberFieldArithmetic.integralIdealsAway m.support'. Direction was established from each sentence rather than assumed: the two remaining citations run the other way and are correctly not dependencies — 'is an export to GlobalQuadraticForms', and 'This is a local theorem: [the Number-Field Arithmetic roadmap] consumes it only after passing to a completion', the latter resolving the apparent mutual dependency between LocalFieldsRamification and NumberFieldArithmetic into supplier and consumer, with no cycle. Calibration: 161 of 211 atlas roadmaps declare at least one prerequisite.
findings.fix: Add the three stated dependencies to the prerequisites fields, which introduces no cycle: QuadraticFormInvariants gains tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification; NumberFieldArithmetic gains tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification; GlobalNumberFields gains tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic. Leave LocalFieldsRamification, GlobalQuadraticForms, Multiquadratic and PolynomialGaloisGroups as they are unless their documents state a dependency this red team did not find — LocalFieldsRamification in particular should stay empty, since its only sibling citation names a consumer. If the area's authors intend prose to be the only record of ordering, that convention should be stated in the area's index, since 76 per cent of the atlas does otherwise and consumers of the graph will assume the field is authoritative.
